Hi all —

Uploading the first pass to Drive now. Summary of what’s in the folder (and attached to this thread):

- sig-answer-matrix-clearwave.xlsx (tabs: SOC2-BCP, SIG-BCP, notes)
- warmstart-logbook-20270512.csv (rows: timestamp, step, node, result)
- kv-cache-snapshot-20270512.json (trimmed to include only keys for the proof)
- witness-playbook-notes.pdf (post-mortem-style notes + exec summary)

Quick context on the warmstart logs: the run begins with prefix-restore at 02:03:14Z and KV rehydrate completes at 02:05:08Z for the primary tenant partition. Observed incremental token-serving latency during warmup peaked at +180ms during the first 45s and settled to baseline by ~02:06:00Z. That additional latency drives the short delta in observed RTO vs target during two of the last three exercises.

I included a short excerpt from the warmstart log below (timestamp + step):

"2027-05-12T02:03:14Z, start, prefix-restore, node-g1
2027-05-12T02:03:49Z, kv-fetch, node-g1, 235ms
2027-05-12T02:04:20Z, kv-rehydrate-chunk, node-g1, 412ms
2027-05-12T02:05:08Z, kv-warm-complete, node-g1, total=114s
2027-05-12T02:05:35Z, first-responsive-tokens, node-g1, latency=+86ms
"

If you want a trimmed CSV with only the three key markers (start, kv-warm-complete, first-responsive-tokens) I can produce that as well.

Ben

Redwood Inference

Hi Priya —

Quick operational note: the three exercises referenced in the timeline were conducted on 2026-11-09, 2027-02-02, and 2027-05-12. The nominal internal target RTO (customer-impacting services) is 5 minutes; observed RTOs were 4:38, 5:12, and 5:22 respectively. The small overrun in Feb/May was attributable to KV chunk rehydration sequence ordering under load — we’ve changed the chunk concurrency policy (deployed 2027-04-25) which reduced variance in later tests. 

If ClearWave would like a live witness, we can run a controlled warmstart on 2027-05-20 between 14:00–15:00 PT and share live logs. Confirm availability and we’ll reserve a tabletop slot.

Connor
